sections.html:
The Lincoln County Register of Deeds is at 206 Gamble Drive, 2nd Floor, Lincolnton, NC 28092. The phone is (704) 736-1744, the fax is (704) 736-8830, and email goes to register@lincolncountync.gov.

The office is open 8:00am to 5:00pm Monday through Friday, except county holidays. Real estate recordings and notary oaths stop at 4:30pm every day, so a deed that arrives at 4:45pm waits for the next business day. If you are driving in from Denver or Maiden on a closing day, plan to arrive well before that cutoff.

Payment is by cash, certified or business check, money order, or debit and credit card. Personal checks are not taken, and cards are not accepted for a recording that contains excise tax. That covers most deed filings, since most sales carry that tax.

The office holds real estate records back to 1769, birth and death records from 1913, and marriage records from 1868. Real estate records and the birth, death and marriage indexes are also searchable online.

For a seller, the useful pieces are the grantor and grantee indexes, recorded deeds of trust, plats and maps, powers of attorney and assumed names. The office also keeps military records and notary public records. Since January 1, 2022 it no longer issues birth certificates for people born outside Lincoln County, so heirs closing out an estate should request those certificates from the county of birth.

  • Deeds and deeds of trust recorded against the parcel.
  • Plats and maps that show boundaries and lot numbers.
  • Powers of attorney used by a signer who is not present.
  • Death records for owners who have died.

A paper deed must follow the state formatting standards in G.S. 161-14, which the office posts on its site. An instrument that misses them is still recorded, but the register collects a $25 fee for a nonstandard document.

Paper formatting standards for recorded instruments
Page elementStandard
Sheet size8 1/2 x 11 or 8 1/2 x 14
Top margin, first pageAt least 3 inches
Other margins, first pageAt least 1/2 inch on three sides
Margins, later pagesAt least 1/2 inch on all sides
Ink and paperBlack on white
Smallest typeNo smaller than 9 points
Sides printedFront only
Instrument typeNamed at the head of page one, under the margin

Pen is allowed for filling blanks or making corrections. If the only defect is print smaller than 9 points, the register may waive the $25 charge when the page is still legible, but the office advises 9 point type to avoid rejection. The standards cover instruments in general, deeds of trust and mortgages, UCC filings, Torrens registration and master forms.

State law fixes the fees. G.S. 161-10 sets a base of $26 for an ordinary instrument of up to 15 pages and $64 for a mortgage or deed of trust of up to 35 pages, with $4 for every page past those limits. Bundling a second instrument into the same document adds $10. Lenders pay nothing when they record a cancellation.

The excise tax is separate. Under G.S. 105-228.30 the rate is $1 per $500 of the price or value, with part of a $500 block rounded up, and the seller must deliver it to the register ahead of recording.

Because card payments are barred for recordings with excise tax, the closing attorney usually brings a firm or trust account check.

Recording fixes the order of claims. Under G.S. 47-18, a deed or sales contract has no force against lien creditors or paying buyers until the register of deeds in the land's county has it on file, and the timing of that filing sets who comes first.

Two practical points follow for a Lincoln County seller. First, confirm that old mortgages show a recorded cancellation before closing, since a lender's payoff letter alone does not clear the index. Second, options, long leases and first-refusal rights are governed by that statute too, so have the closing attorney look for them.

Property taxes are ordinarily prorated at closing by the closing attorney, so ask to see the proration on the settlement statement.

Lincoln County has 98,654 residents, up 13.7 percent since 2020, and 41,865 housing units. Owners occupy 78.9 percent of homes, and the typical home is worth $321,000. With 785 building permits in 2025, new construction competes with resales. Fire district rates differ across the county, including Alexis, Crouse, Denver, East Lincoln, High Shoals and North Brook, so read the tax rate sheet before you quote a net figure to a buyer.

sections.h2: What to bring to the Lincolnton counter
sections.html:
Bring the signed, notarized deed, the excise tax, the page fee and a plan for the receipt. If a lender is paying off a loan, line up the cancellation so the old deed of trust comes off the index promptly.

  • A deed that meets the margin and type size standards, with the instrument type printed at the top.
  • Payment in an accepted form, remembering that cards are not taken when excise tax is due.
  • Arrival before 4:30pm, the daily cutoff for real estate recordings.
  • The full list of owners, spouses and heirs who must sign.
  • A look at the tax rate sheet: the county rate is 0.499 per $100 for 2026/2027, and the City of Lincolnton adds 0.5000 for a total of 0.9990.

Tax matters live in a different office. Collections are handled by the Lincoln County Tax Department, and the 2027 revaluation takes effect January 1, 2027, so ask that department about current-year balances.

sections.h2: A cash sale and the recording step
sections.html:
Selling for cash does not change what the register needs. The deed still has to be signed, notarized and formatted correctly, the excise tax still has to be paid, and the closing attorney still delivers it before 4:30pm. What a cash sale can remove is the wait for a lender, which helps if the house has liens, tenants or repairs you would rather not tackle.

If a prior loan is paid off at closing, the cancellation recorded afterward is what clears the index. Ask the attorney to confirm it has been recorded, and keep a copy with your closing papers.

A rough order for closing day in Lincolnton: the attorney reviews the deed against the formatting table, you sign before a notary, the buyer funds, and the attorney brings the deed and a firm or trust account check for the excise tax and page fees to Gamble Drive. After recording, the old lender's cancellation follows, and recording it costs nothing.

faqs.q: What time does the Lincoln County Register of Deeds stop recording?
faqs.a: Real estate recordings and notary oaths stop at 4:30pm every day, even though the office stays open until 5:00pm. Arrive before 4:30pm on closing day.

faqs.q: Can I pay the Lincoln County recording fee with a credit card?
faqs.a: A card works for most services but not for a recording that contains excise tax. Use cash, a certified or business check, or a money order, and do not bring a personal check.

faqs.q: How far back do Lincoln County real estate records go?
faqs.a: Real estate records go back to 1769, and the same years are searchable online. Birth and death indexes start in 1913 and marriage indexes in 1868.

faqs.q: What happens if my deed is not formatted correctly in Lincoln County?
faqs.a: The register will still record it, but it collects a $25 nonstandard document fee. Black ink on white paper, correct margins and 9 point type avoid the charge.

faqs.q: Where do I get my Lincoln County property tax balance before I sell?
faqs.a: Call the Lincoln County Tax Department or use its online payment page. Taxes are due September 1 and become delinquent after January 5, and the closing attorney normally prorates the current year.
